sun.declination_note: Northern-summer solstice: the Sun reaches the table's sun_elev_max_deg (69.04 deg = 90 - 22.5 + 1.54) at local noon, in the south. Illustrative choice of season; other seasons change the noon Sun by at most 3.1 deg.
sun.window_note: One lunar daytime, from shortly after sunrise (Sun 1.5 deg up) to shortly before sunset: 178 deg of the 181.3 deg of hour angle between flat-horizon sunrise and sunset (14.6 of the 14.9 Earth days of daylight). The other half of the 29.53-day cycle is night (shaded on the graph).

earth_visibility.decision: Not drawn. At its mean position (the sub-Earth point at 0 N 0 E; elevation 90 deg minus the 22.8 deg arc from the site, az 170.9 deg; parallax and libration ignored, a geometric estimate) the Earth stands about 67 deg up in the south, above the camera's field of view for most of the video.

array.assumption: Illustrative engineering shape, not a real design: short mast, hub 2.4 m above ground; two wings of 3 hinged panels, each panel 2.0 m x 1.2 m (total 14.4 m2), that unfold upwards and end flat (horizontal, tilt 0 deg), as the mission's irradiance (a horizontal surface) assumes. No tracking.

render.lighting_note: Sun: one parallel light of fixed intensity (3.2 in renderer units, chosen so that the high noon Sun does not saturate the light-grey ground); terrain shadows from the real SLDEM2015 horizons; 3.5 % uniform fill (assumption). Display exposure (a camera setting; the light and the power are not changed): min(8, max(1, sin 25° / sin h)), h = Sun elevation; stated on screen whenever it is above 1.25.

card.title: Earth analog and lunar twin: solar panels, pair number 1
card.subtitle: Suitability 96.9, similarity 99.99, final 98.45. The lunar cell lies in the low equatorial plains (the maria), the Solar panels zone: within 30° of the equator and at or below −1,200 m. Values from the project tables (1-degree cells); each carries its level.

rows.label: Sunlight above the atmosphere
rows.earth_note: top of the atmosphere, formula from latitude

card.legend: Sunlight above the atmosphere: on Earth, the annual-mean daily sunlight on a horizontal surface at the top of the atmosphere, from the cell's latitude (a formula); on the Moon, the table's surface irradiance (horizontal, S0 = 1361 W/m², averaged over the whole lunar cycle, nights included). Sunlight reaching the ground on Earth: WorldClim 2.1, modelled (non-commercial licence). A panel at the Earth site receives only the sunlight that reaches the ground. The Solar panels similarity is saturated. Sunlight above the atmosphere depends on latitude only, so almost every Earth point finds many cells of the equatorial maria that match it almost exactly: its twin is the best of a median of about 1,840 candidate cells that pass the tolerances, 78 % of the 6,360 pairs score 99 or more and 514 show 100.00. Here a high similarity says that the pair is within the tolerances, not that it is closer than another pair: read the real differences shown beside it (sunlight above the atmosphere, slope and roughness). Among the 100 best-ranked points the similarity only goes from 99.88 to 100.00, so their order follows suitability.

pair_values.source: app/public/data/v2/explain.json, missions.solar item with rank 1; similarity.json (display rule of the share lost, saturation note, lunar day); missions.json and mission_zones.json (zone); variables.json and missions.json similarity sides (levels). prepare.py checks every value here against those files, and render.js runs that check before it renders.
pair_values.pair_sentence: This pair is matched on sunlight above the atmosphere: 9.6 kWh/m²/day at the top of Earth's atmosphere here and 9.6 kWh/m²/day on the lunar surface. At the Earth site only 6.2 of those 9.6 kWh/m²/day reach the ground (35 % is lost in the atmosphere), while the Moon has no atmosphere and its day lasts 29.5 Earth days, about half of them in darkness. Terrain (slope and roughness) is a secondary criterion.

Among the 100 best-ranked points the similarity only goes from 99.88 to 100.00, so their order follows suitability.

captions.cue_rule: Cue boundaries are the frames where the panel status changes (render.js --timeline), plus mid-phase cues and the closing card; render.js refuses to write captions if the status changes inside a cue.
